g.text: On this page you will find:
– 3D-print files for the frame, the lift and the gripper
SCAN FOR DOCS, CODE AND LESSONS
Design files are published. Print it, fix it, improve it, share it.
– 3 x 18650 lithium cells (not included) and a USB-C charger
– A computer or tablet with a browser, or the Arduino IDE
– Charge the robot fully before the first lesson
– Raise the lift by hand before you switch the robot on
Plastal-Bot Builders is a Lusaka makerspace that teaches robotics, coding
and fabrication to learners and teachers across Zambia. RoboCore is our own
controller family, designed so a class can build, program and repair its robots
WORKSHOPS · TEACHER TRAINING · ROBOTICS CLUBS · FABRICATION
Share what your class builds, find lesson plans and compare notes with other
schools. Replacement parts and add-on sensors are available from us; the
design files are published so you can also print and fix parts yourself.
LESSON PLANS · FORUM · SPARE PARTS · DESIGN FILES
Encoder motors DG01D-E (2, on the robot)
Wheels 56 mm, TPU tyres (2, on the robot)
V-wheels 24 mm, with bearings (4, on the robot)
Micro servos MG90S (2, on the robot)
Rear deck, Technic grid (on the robot)
For replacement parts and add-on sensors visit plastalbotbuilders.com/robocore
Designed and built in Zambia by Plastal-Bot Builders, Lusaka

INSIDE (mirrored: prints on the back of the outside sheet). RoboCore mailer box, roll-end tuck-top, outer 303 x 213 x 91 mm, E-flute 1.5 mm. Print 1:1; navy solid = cut, grey dashed = fold. Bar = 100 mm.
